title: Global strict transform is a closed subscheme
statement:
Under the data of
[def-nagata-strict-transform-closed-chart-model], the constructed chart
model $Y^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$ is a closed
subscheme of $Y\times_XX'$ and agrees with the strict transform of
[def-nagata-strict-transform].

proof.text:
The chartwise closed immersions agree on overlaps by
[lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-cocycle]; therefore their ideals
glue to a global quasi-coherent ideal, with localization compatibility
supplied by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-chart-localization-data].
On each chart the quotient removes
exactly the sections supported on the exceptional divisor, so the resulting
closed subscheme is the scheme-theoretic closure of the preserved open and
hence is the strict transform.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
Under the data of
[def-nagata-strict-transform-closed-chart-model], let
$Y^{\mathrm{st}}\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the strict transform of $Y$
relative to $X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$ ([def-nagata-strict-transform]).
For every chart datum $c=(U,V,a)$, the restriction of the ideal of
$Y^{\mathrm{st}}$ along $\iota_c$ is $\Gamma_{(a)}(C_a(A,B,I))$; that is,
$Y^{\mathrm{st}}$ meets the chart $\operatorname{Spec}(C_a(A,B,I))$ in
$\operatorname{Spec}(C_a^{\mathrm{st}}(A,B,I))$. Consequently the chart
model $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$ is the ideal of
$Y^{\mathrm{st}}$, so $Y^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}=Y^{\mathrm{st}}$
as closed subschemes of $Y\times_XX'$, and the restriction of
$\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$ along every chart $\iota_c$ is
$\Gamma_{(a)}(C_a(A,B,I))$.

proof.text:
Let $\Omega\subseteq Y\times_XX'$ be the open part lying over
$X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, so that $Y^{\mathrm{st}}$ is the
scheme-theoretic image of $\Omega\hookrightarrow Y\times_XX'$. Fix a chart
datum $c=(U,V,a)$ and put $C=C_a(A,B,I)$. The preimage of $V(\mathcal I)$
in $\operatorname{Spec}(C)$ is cut out by $IC$, which is generated by $a$
because $I\,A[I/a]=(a)$ ([lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal]).
Hence $\iota_c^{-1}(\Omega)=D(a)=\operatorname{Spec}(C_a)$, which is affine.
The chart images cover $Y\times_XX'$ (the $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ cover
$Y$ over the $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and the $a$-charts cover the
blow-up of each $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$), so
$\Omega\hookrightarrow Y\times_XX'$ is quasi-compact and the ideal of its
scheme-theoretic image is computed chart by chart and commutes with
restriction to the open charts ([lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc]). On
the chart it is the kernel of $C\to C_a$, which is $\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$ by
[lemma-nagata-power-torsion-kernel-localization]. This proves the
chartwise statement.

Let $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}$ be the ideal of $Y^{\mathrm{st}}$. By the
chartwise statement $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}$ satisfies the condition in
the definition of the chart model, so
$\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}\subseteq\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$.
Conversely, the restriction of $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}$
to every chart is contained in $\Gamma_{(a)}(C)$, which is the restriction
of $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}$; since the charts cover $Y\times_XX'$ and
inclusions of quasi-coherent ideals can be checked on an open cover,
$\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}_{\mathrm{chart}}\subseteq\mathcal J^{\mathrm{st}}$.
Hence the two ideals are equal, and the last assertion is the chartwise
statement once more.
